direction_name: NEGATIVE SPACE (final): a cut-paper noir where the extra guest is the hole
pitch: The film is a cut-paper noir. The six friends are crisp black silhouettes, each shot is lit by a single lamp, and every line of dialogue is designed type that moves the way its speaker does: Scott types and deletes like a text he never sends, Angelo deals his words like cards, Kay's lines fog on like breath on glass. The extra guest is never drawn. It shows up only as something missing: an empty seat at Scott's right, a count that comes out wrong, letters cut out of the darkness that glow with the fire still to come. Each time someone is lost the frame narrows, until the explosion tears it open, and the last light in the film is a hand made of fire, holding Scott's.
why_this_direction:
All three judges picked NEGATIVE SPACE (aggregate 125.5, against 113 and 107) because it is the only direction where one rule covers the story, the horror, the dialogue and the build.

1. The story. The screenplay is about subtraction: a seat no one is in, a voice from nowhere, 'No second figure is visible.' Here the paper world is laid over a hidden layer of firelight, and the extra guest can only remove things. It cuts holes through the paper, opens gaps in compositions and changes things between frames. So the thing that is never seen is made of the fire that ends the film. The explosion briefly inverts the whole world into that material, and the last image is a hand of that light. 'Two.' carries relief and dread together.

2. The buildability risks. Silhouettes remove the brief's biggest risk, procedurally drawn faces. Profiles merge in one ink, so simple rigs read as seamless. A hand-authored library of silhouette hand poses can reach a premium finish where shaded procedural hands can't. Flat three-tone fire looks designed rather than simulated.

3. Grafts. This final spec fixes every story deviation the judges found (six hands, the ring of four in the hand circle, the LATER beat, handedness, the VOICE typeface logic, the call timer, Kay's matte step) and takes the strongest ideas from the other two directions:
- From RECOUNT: Scott's caret that types and deletes like an unsent text, the gas hiss planted subliminally, Marina's empty wine ring, Kay's afterimage on the wall, the dormant call line that becomes the scream.
- From ONE ROD TOO MANY: the VOICE borrowing the face of the friend it mimics, Kay animated on ones, burn holes that never heal, the single-take standoff, the second heartbeat that locks on 'Two.', and the objects left behind.
None of this needs a second look; the grafts are expressed in the same ink, light and holes.
rendering_technique:
ENGINE
- One 1920x1080 Canvas 2D surface drawn by a pure function render(t). Frame f = round(t*24).
- Target runtime 13:44 (824 s, 19,776 frames).
- No Math.random, Date or performance.now anywhere in the render path. All variation comes from mulberry32 seeded by hash32(shotId, elementId[, f]).
- A shot table drives everything: {id, master, tIn, tOut, camera keys, light rig, cast poses, dialogue ids, extra events, matte aspect}. drawShot(ctx, shot, localT) is pure.
- Character poses are quantised to 12 fps: tq = floor(t*12)/12, giving a cut-paper cadence on twos. Kay (real Kay only) and panic beats sample at 24 fps. Camera, light, type, particles and post run on ones.
- Preview renders at 960x540 by ctx.setTransform(0.5,...). All geometry is authored in 1920x1080 units, so preview and export are identical apart from scale.
- Export: Puppeteer drives headless Chromium at 1920x1080, stepping t = n/24. Frames come out either as canvas.toBlob PNG piped to ffmpeg (-c:v libx264 -crf 14 -pix_fmt yuv420p -r 24), or through the WebCodecs VideoEncoder (avc1.640028) with mp4-muxer.
- Audio is rendered separately (see sound palette) and muxed with ffmpeg as AAC 320k.

DATA MODEL
- All character, set, hand and Extra geometry is stored as arrays of cubic Bezier points, never as opaque Path2D, so edge noise, shadow matrices, rim offsets, the throat arc and the hand family have vertex access.
- Each frame, every shape is flattened to segments of about 6 px, displaced, then built into a fresh Path2D.
- Dialogue lives in dialogue.json, generated by a parser straight from the screenplay text: {id, speaker, text, tIn, behaviour, anchor, interruptAt}. A lint step fails the build if any on-screen string differs from the screenplay.
  - '--' is rendered as an em dash glyph (U+2014).
  - Straight quotes are rendered as curly (U+201C/U+201D/U+2019).
  - Every face is checked for those glyphs at load.
- A type-only animatic (every verbatim line at its hold time, on ink, with landing sounds) is built and timed BEFORE any art. It locks the runtime at 13:44 +/-20 s.

LAYER STACK (offscreen canvases, back to front)
L0 BACKING FIRE (the lightbox)
- A full-frame fbm value-noise field (4 octaves) computed at 240x135, scrolled upward at 0.35 frame-heights/s, mapped through a ramp fire-outer #A9280B -> ember #FF7A24 -> ember-core #FFF1CF (ramp position = noise^0.8), then upscaled with imageSmoothingQuality 'high'.
- It is rendered every frame and is ALWAYS fully covered by the paper world, except where the Extra cuts through (L8).

L1 LIGHT FIELD
- Each shot has one motivated source: {pos, palette[3], radii[3]} or a trapezoid cone. Defaults:
  - living-room lamp: radii 300/520/860 px;
  - dining pendant top-down: rings 260/420/620;
  - hood cone: a trapezoid, 180 px wide at the lamp and 760 px at the floor.
- Light is three posterised flat bands (for example tungsten #F2A93B / tungsten-mid #A4611F / tungsten-low #4B2B13) over soot. There are no smooth gradients.
- Each band boundary gets a 2 px screen-print seam: a ring clipped to the boundary and filled with a 4x4 Bayer-dither pattern of the outer colour.
- Light radius flickers +/-4% with the same noise that drives fire whenever fire is present.

L2 SET
- Walls, frames, the round table, chairs, stove, fence and grass are filled ink #0D0A09 or soot #1E1714.
- Countable sets are generated by code so their counts are exact and animatable: glasses, chairs, card piles, knobs, tiles, fence slats, windows, footprints.

L3 CAST SHADOWS
- Each silhouette is redrawn through a shadow matrix (scale about the light position plus a shear onto the floor or wall plane) and filled ink at 85% over the light field.
- The Extra never casts one. Fake-Kay fragments never cast one.

L4 CHARACTERS
- 14-joint rig: pelvis, spine, neck, head, and shoulder/elbow/wrist and hip/knee/ankle on each side.
- Per character there are authored Bezier parts: profile head, hair, torso (profile / three-quarter back / front), signature attachments.
- Limbs are tapered capsules driven by analytic two-bone IK.
- Everything is filled in ONE ink, so overlaps merge seamlessly.
- Profile head = an 18-point contour with named control points: brow, nose bridge, nose tip, nose base, upper lip, mouth corner notch, lower lip, chin, jaw angle, nape.
- MICRO-ACTING, all pure functions of t:
  - browRaise -1..1: moves the 3 brow points 0..6 px along the normal.
  - jawOpen 0..6 deg.
  - lipPress 0..2 px.
  - smile 0..1: cheek vertex +2 px, mouth-corner notch deepens 1.5 px.
  - headTilt +/-12 deg.
  - breath: chest rise 2-4 px at 0.25-0.4 Hz baseline, 0.8-1.2 Hz in fear.
  - shoulderLift 0..8 px.
- CUT-PAPER EDGE: every flattened vertex is displaced along its normal by frozen seeded noise of +/-0.7 px. From the hand circle onward it re-seeds every 2 frames at +/-0.4 px, rising to +/-1.4 px in the kitchen ('edge boil').
- RIM LIGHT: fill the path in the light colour, then fill the same path in ink, translated 3 px away from the light and clipped to the original. The result is a 2-5 px crescent. Rim width is a dramatic control (Angelo 4 -> 1 px; everyone thins in the kitchen).
- SECONDARY MOTION is closed-form, never stateful: each spring channel (Deena's ponytail k70/c7, Christof's curls k40/c5, Angelo's jacket hem k55/c6, Kay's wet hair ends k60/c9) is x(t) = sum over keyed pose changes i with t_i <= t of A_i * e^(-zeta*w*(t - t_i)) * cos(w_d*(t - t_i)), where A_i is the parent joint's angular step at key i. This is a pure function of t.

L4b HANDS
- A library of 18 hand poses authored as Bezier arrays at 4x and scaled per character (Angelo x1.08): open-relaxed, crisp-scoop, card-pinch, deal-flick, fan, point, wrist-grip, clasp-L, clasp-R, slap-flat-on-card, throat-cover, limp-palm-up, knife-grip, lighter-thumb, shoulder-squeeze, tremble-on-shoulder, phone-hold, glass-stem.
- THE EXTRA HAND FAMILY: three LEFT-hand poses built on one 22-point base (neutral long fingers, no rings, no knuckle detail): PRESS (the sixth card), PRINT (the handprint, splayed), CLASP (the ending). They are similar, never highlighted as identical.

L4c GRAPHIC EYES
- The only interior facial feature, used in exactly 8 extreme close-ups (listed under the cast and the beat map).
- Almond: two quadratic arcs, eye width 0.22 of frame height, filled card-paper #EFE5D0 at 88%.
- Iris disc: radius 0.38 x eye height, in ink with a 2 px rim in the key colour.
- One or two catchlights in flash-white #F8F4EA.
- Upper-lid arc morphs aperture 0.15..1.0 (ease cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1), 160 ms).

L5 SIGNATURE ACCENTS (small, bright, hand-placed): hoop arc, cigarette sliver, ring glints, rain beads, biscuit disc, lip mark, lighter glint.

L6 ATMOSPHERE
- Light cones composited 'screen' at 0.08-0.14.
- 40-80 dust motes as closed-form drift: p = p0 + v*t + 6 px * sin(0.7t + phase).
- Rain in 3 depth layers of 1 px diagonal strokes.
- Gas haze: the stove region is redrawn in 3 px horizontal strips offset by 1.5*sin(0.09y + 5.1t), tinted gas-blue #5D8DF2 at 8-14%.

L7 TYPE
- A per-glyph kinetic engine. Glyph x positions come from measureText of cumulative prefixes, so kerning is kept (ctx.fontKerning = 'normal').
- Tracking uses ctx.letterSpacing. Scott's width uses ctx.fontStretch keywords on the variable Roboto Flex face.
- Lines are depth-sorted (a line can sit behind a silhouette), can be projected onto set planes with setTransform (words dealt onto the table in top-downs), and can be clipped by set edges (the oven door).
- Matte-aware layout: type never enters the matte except where the rules move it there (see motion rules).
- Tabular figures are laid out manually: each digit is centred in a fixed cell equal to the widest digit's advance.

L8 KNOCKOUT
- Every Extra mark (VOICE letters, title 'ONE', the throat arc, the handprint, the final hand, the inversion frames) is drawn with globalCompositeOperation 'destination-out' into the merged paper layer (L1-L7, already grained), so L0 fire shows through with NO grain. The holes look too clean.
- Knockout depth (alpha of the cut) is a parameter: 100% for the VOICE, 35% for the handprint.
- Each master set keeps a list of its knockout scars. They persist and glow at 6% the next time that set appears, rising 1% per minute.

L9 POST
- Halation: lamp cores, fire, glints, knockouts and bright type are drawn into a separate 480x270 emissive buffer, blurred with ctx.filter 'blur(4px)', tinted #FF4A1C, then upscaled and composited 'screen' at 0.22. Nothing is thresholded at full resolution.
- Grain: 8 seeded 512x512 tiles chosen by f mod 8, composited 'overlay' at 0.06 (Act 1) rising to 0.10 (kitchen).
- A static procedural paper-fibre texture (fbm plus 3,000 fibre strokes, generated once) composited 'multiply' at 0.04.
- Radial vignette to 0.55 ink.
- Gate weave of +/-0.5 px, stepped at 12 fps.
- Animated letterbox mattes.
- Wine flashes: 2 frames of #6E1222 composited 'multiply' at 25%.

FIRE
- Flat three-tone flame tongues: closed Beziers with 6-9 control points riding 2D value noise.
- Layers: fire-outer #A9280B, ember #FF7A24, ember-core #FFF1CF.
- Embers are closed-form particles: p(tau) = p0 + v0*tau + 0.5*a*tau^2 + curl(p0, tau)*18 px, with a = (0, -40 px/s^2) and drag folded into v0*(1 - e^(-1.2 tau))/1.2.

BURN-THROUGH
- A 480x270 fbm threshold mask: a pixel is burnt where noise(x,y)*0.35 + dist(x,y,origin)/R(t) < 1.
- Edge bands: a 14 px ember band and a 6 px char band in #2A1208.
- It is upscaled with smoothing and used for the cold-open slit, the curtain, and the mattes burning away in the explosion.

PHONE PHOTO
- The same renderer redraws the four-figure flash composition into a 360x640 offscreen canvas, lit frontally with flash-white figures and hard ink shadows, so it matches the room for free.

CACHING
- Static set layers, blurred backgrounds and shadow passes are cached as ImageBitmap per (shotId, scale). Expect 0.12-0.3 s per frame headless, or 40-100 minutes per full export.

MASTERS AND BUDGET
- About 140 shots built from 14 master set-ups:
  - M1 front door (locked, symmetrical)
  - M2 living-room frieze
  - M3 table top-down
  - M4 table profile two-shot
  - M5 kitchen doorway from the dining area
  - M6 one-point corridor
  - M7 kitchen stove
  - M8 oven under-light
  - M9 tile floor top-down
  - M10 back door exterior
  - M11 yard wide
  - M12 yard close
  - M13 hand inserts in a lamp pool
  - M14 phone screen
- About 85% of shots reuse a master camera exactly; the remaining 15% are bespoke (oven interior, hand-circle top-down, explosion).

SEATING LOCK, used by every table shot (clock positions in top-down, Scott at the bottom): Christof 2, Angelo 12, Deena 10, Marina 8, Scott 6, Kay 4. Scott's right = screen-right in top-down. The Extra's gap is the sector from Kay's chair (4 o'clock) to Scott (6 o'clock): the seventh pile, the sixth card, fake-Kay, the fifth glass, the empty roll-call corner and the photographer's spot all fall in it. The roll-call order follows from the geometry:
- 'left' runs Scott -> Marina -> Deena -> Angelo -> Scott, and the Extra at 4 o'clock has Scott on its left.
- 'right' runs Scott -> Angelo -> Deena -> Marina -> Scott, and the Extra has Angelo on its right.

PRE-PRODUCTION GATES (both must pass before shots are built)
(1) A silhouette lineup: every character must be identifiable in pure ink at 120 px tall.
(2) A 60-second Act 1 test cut (Deena/Angelo arrival plus 'Sit down, Scott') that has to read as funny and warm without faces. The 8 graphic-eye shots are tested in it, and any that look uncanny are cut back to profile micro-acting.

colour_arc.light: The ink house sits against yard-night. Its five windows are flat three-tone fire, and maximum saturation exists only inside them. A phone-white rim lights Scott's left ear and cheek. Faint strobe bars cover at most 10% of the fence. At the frame-right edge where his free right hand is cropped, a 6% warm flicker plays and is never explained. About 70% of the frame is ink.

A hard cut into full tungsten in three posterised bands. In the title, six ink bars stand on a tungsten field. 'ONE' is knocked out to the backing fire, the audience's first one-second exposure to the Extra's material.

Warm hall light in three bands. The door rectangle is rain-slate with rain-silver streaks, and every opening lets cold in. After the second CLICK no cold light appears until the phone in the yard. About 40% ink.
The warmest point of the film: large lamp pools, wine in the glasses, card-paper accents. At most four colours per shot, excluding ink and type. About 40-45% ink.

colour_arc.section: Card table: seven hands to five cards (2:53-5:01)
colour_arc.light: One pendant throws three hard rings on the round table, with ink beyond. Card-blue backs and ivory faces are the strongest graphics. Kay's lip mark is the only true red. About 55% ink.

Tungsten drains to tungsten-tired on the crash frame, and the pool shrinks 15%. The kitchen doorway glows a wrong hood-yellow. The untouched lip mark is the most saturated thing in the room. About 70% ink.
A top-down pool frames exactly the table, and faces are lost. The backing fire appears indoors for the first time, through the VOICE's knockout letters. About 75% ink.

The flash gives 3 frames of flash-white with a 6-frame decay: the four friends become paper-white shapes with hard ink shadows, lit frontally by whoever took it. The film's maximum contrast. Then phone-white lights faces from below.
No key light: only the unbroken under-door line, with no feet behind it, and the far hood-yellow glow. Figures are rim-only. Kay's 8% afterimage sits on the wall. About 85% ink.

A hood-yellow cone lights the stove over ink and soot checker tiles, with a gas-blue haze. Opening the oven flips the key to under-lighting from the bulb. Blood is the wine's darker cousin. Deena's throat glows ember-core and ember for 4 frames before it turns to blood. The handprint is a 35% knockout. About 85% ink.

About 92% ink. Angelo stands at the edge of the hood cone; behind Scott is the back-door rectangle. The lighter glint is the brightest point in frame. The handprint scar and the throat cut leak ember through the edge of the jacket.

3 frames of blast-white, then 4 frames of inversion (ink becomes ember-core, light becomes ink), then full fire while the mattes burn away. The inversion's mean luminance is held within 20% of blast-white for flash safety.

Fire rims Scott's back. Strobe red and blue bars (0.8 Hz each) slide through the fence slats. Phone-white lights his face. Ash type gives way to amber on 'Two.' Over the last 20 s everything sinks to ink except the hand-shaped knockout of fire, the last light in the film.

fonts.role: The title 'ONE TOO MANY' and the end card. Ultra-condensed caps set at 300-600 px, so each letter reads as a vertical bar, like the bodies. Each glyph gets frozen seeded jitter of +/-0.6 deg and +/-2 px baseline

characters.name: Scott
characters.build:
Base height H = 1.00; a full figure in a medium is 454 px.
- Head 0.135H tall; skull ellipse 0.115H wide; neck 0.045H.
- Shoulder line at 0.82H from the floor. Shoulder width 0.235H with rounded 0.035H deltoids (soft shoulders, never square).
- Torso 0.30H, hip width 0.19H. Arm 0.42H (upper arm 0.19, forearm 0.17, hand 0.06, hand library x1.00). Leg 0.47H.
- Permanent 6 deg forward lean from the hips, with the neck a further 4 deg forward: a man always about to stand up.
- Hair: a neat cap 0.012H thick following the skull from brow to nape, plus the COWLICK, a 3-vertex tapered spike at the crown, 0.028H tall, 0.008H base, raked 30 deg back.
- Shirt: two collar-point triangles (0.018H) break the neckline. Sleeves rolled once give a 0.012H cuff bump at 55% down each forearm. Straight trousers.
- Socks all night: heel-less rounded feet (ellipse 0.13H x 0.035H) with no sole step.
- Profile: soft round nose tip (radius 0.006H), mild chin.
- Yard variant:
  - The right sleeve is torn to a jagged edge (12 seeded vertices, +/-0.010H).
  - The hem is scorched (sawtooth +/-0.006H).
  - The LEFT forearm (the phone arm) is blistered: its rim light is replaced by a ragged ember #FF7A24 rim with 0.003H noise.
  - The phone is always in his LEFT hand at his left ear; his free RIGHT hand is on the gap side.
- Graphic-eye close-ups:
  - E0: cold open, staring at the house.
  - E2: 'What about Saturday?'
  - E7: the 'Me.' to 'Two.' reprise.
characters.signature_detail: The cowlick, the hover lean and the socks. The cowlick is the first thing the rim light catches in any shot of him. In his type, the signature is a blinking caret: the text he started on Monday and never sent.
characters.motion_trait:
He hovers and never fully settles.
- Idle sway 0.8 Hz, +/-3 px.
- Every pose lands, then makes a 6 px 'tidy' correction 160 ms later.
- Hand fidgets every 1.2-2.0 s on a seeded schedule: crumbs, glasses, coasters.
- Starts are hesitant: a 3-frame anticipation, then cubic-bezier(0.55,0.06,0.68,0.19).
- In fear, a 9 Hz, +/-1.5 px hand tremor (the knife blade shows it).
- In the yard, only breathing: a 4 px rise at 0.25 Hz. On 'Two.' his shoulders drop 6 px over 400 ms, cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1).

dialogue.weight_style: wght 460, upright. Under stress wght 560. 'Me.' is wght 300; 'Two.' is wght 420.
dialogue.size_and_case:
48 px, sentence case, tracking 0.
- 'Where is it?' and 'No.' are 72 px.
- 'Me.' and 'Two.' are 160 px.
- Width steps with ctx.fontStretch: normal through Act 1; semi-condensed after the crash; condensed after Deena dies; extra-condensed in the standoff and on 'Me.'; back to normal on 'Two.'
dialogue.placement:
Left-aligned in the negative space on his lit side, 40-90 px off his profile, always over ink or on an ink knock-behind.
- From the 2.39 matte step onward his lines sit in the TOP matte band, x-aligned to his head position and clamped 96 px from the frame edges.
- In the yard, 'Me.' and 'Two.' are centred in the sky above the house.
dialogue.entry:
Typed with a caret: a 2 px x 0.9 em type-scott bar, after a 120 ms hesitation, then 38 ms per character. Each character lands with a soft haptic tick.
- 'Me.' and 'Two.' type at a deliberate 140 ms per character, with no jitter.
dialogue.hold_and_exit:
Hold for max(0.9 s, 0.35 s + 55 ms per character) after typing ends. Then the line is DELETED backwards at 8 ms per character, like a draft he won't send.
- Interrupted lines ('I didn't--', 'You want me to--', 'You don't have to--', 'Angelo--') type up to the dash. An invisible vertical edge then guillotines the dash, which drops 20 px and vanishes in 4 frames, and the remainder deletes normally.
- In his silences with Kay (the doorway, after 'What about Saturday?') a bare caret blinks with no text, 530 ms per cycle.
- 'I--' in the cold open blinks its caret until the seventh blink, which is the cut.
- 'Two.' is the only Scott line never deleted: the caret stops after the full stop and disappears, and the line stays until the fade.
dialogue.emotion_modulation:
Stress tightens tracking from 0 to -40, raises weight from 460 to 560, and adds baseline jitter that grows from 0 to +/-2 px at 12 Hz.
- Width notches down one fontStretch keyword per loss: after the crash, after Deena, in the standoff.
- Colour: type-scott amber until the explosion; ash #9A9088 throughout the yard; 'Two.' returns to amber on the exact frame his shoulders drop.
- The unwritten address appears in the yard as a row of five ash redaction bars, typed and deleted, with no letters.
dialogue.sample_line: I was going to text you about Saturday.

characters.name: Deena
characters.build:
Height H = 0.95.
- Head 0.135H, chin raised 4 deg. Straight spine with 0 deg lean.
- Shoulders 0.22H, near-square. Fitted top.
- Wide-leg trousers flare to 0.27H at the hem, giving a clean triangular lower silhouette.
- HIGH PONYTAIL: rooted 0.03H above the skull at the crown-back. A tapered teardrop 0.17H long x 0.05H wide on a 2-segment closed-form spring chain (pivots at the root and at 45%).
- HOOP EARRING: a stroked ellipse 0.032H x 0.034H, 2.5 px stroke in a medium shot. It is the only stroked element on her, and the rim light catches it as a ring-gold arc.
- Profile: straight nose, defined lips, narrow eye.
- Graphic-eye close-up E5: her eyes fix on Angelo, disbelieving.
characters.signature_detail: The high ponytail, which is what the Extra grips, paying off Scott's 'I saw her hair--'. Plus the bright hoop arc.
characters.motion_trait:
Decisive. She snaps pose to pose in 4 frames (2 in-betweens on twos) with cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), and never hovers.
- At idle she is almost perfectly still, so the ponytail (spring k70/c7) is the live element: it swings 2-3 times after every head turn.
- She points with a straight arm.
- Frightened, she freezes completely, and only the ponytail keeps moving.

dialogue.weight_style: Archivo Black 400, upright. Softened lines in Archivo 500.
dialogue.placement:
On her side of the frame, 30-70 px from her profile, sitting level on a real horizontal of the set (table edge, counter).
- Off-screen lines slide in from the frame edge already cropped, like 'Kay! Save yourself. He's rearranged the whole room.'
dialogue.entry:
Hard cut-on: the whole line appears on one frame at 103% scale and settles to 100% over 2 frames with a 2 px shake.
- On 'Who's that for?' and 'Count those.' a 3 px type-deena POINTER RULE draws from the line's end to its target (pile seven; the fifth pile) in 6 frames and ends in a 6 px dot.
- Her 'almost comments, decides not to' is a type-deena text cursor that blinks for 6 frames and dies, with no words.
dialogue.hold_and_exit:
Hold for max(0.9 s, 0.35 s + 55 ms per character). Hard cut-off with no fade: once she's said it, it's said.

characters.name: The Extra / VOICE (O.S.)
characters.build:
NONE. It is never a positive shape: no ink, no outline, no shadow, no reflection, no eyes.
- Its only geometry is subtractive: knockout letters, the short throat arc, and the LEFT-hand family (PRESS, PRINT, CLASP).
- The sixth hand on the sixth card is the exception: unrimmed ink whose forearm emerges from the unlit ink beyond the lamp ring at Scott's right and never joins a body.
- It always sits in the gap sector at Scott's right (Kay's chair, 4 to 6 o'clock in top-down).
characters.signature_detail: It is always on Scott's right. It acts only between frames or across cuts. The holes it cuts never heal: each master set keeps its scars and shows them faintly the next time it appears.
characters.motion_trait: It never moves on screen. Its actions happen across cuts or while Scott looks away. The only on-screen effects are Deena's throat arc and the snap of her ponytail, and even there the effect moves while the cause stays invisible.

dialogue.font: Borrowed: the face of the friend whose line it is mimicking. The first 'Scott.' is in Oswald 500, Angelo's, pre-echoing his own 'Scott.' a moment later. The soft 'Angelo.' is in Archivo Black, Deena's, echoing her 'Angelo.' that stopped the cards.
dialogue.weight_style: Knockout: globalCompositeOperation 'destination-out' through the grained paper layer, revealing ungrained backing fire (ember-core centre, ember rim, live flicker) with halation. It is never filled with colour.
dialogue.size_and_case: 'Scott.' is 52 px at 100% knockout depth. The soft 'Angelo.' is 30 px at 60% depth.
dialogue.placement: World-locked to the empty corner of the hand circle at 4 o'clock (Kay's empty place), on the table plane, never next to a speaker. It ignores camera shake.
dialogue.entry: None. Full opacity on its first frame.
dialogue.hold_and_exit: Holds about 0.9 s, then disappears on the next cut. It then persists as a 6% scorched perforation in the table plane in every later shot of the dining set.
dialogue.emotion_modulation: None. Its 'emotion' is the sound hole: every bus except the 7th-harmonic pair drops to digital silence for the word.

the_extra_rules: RULE ZERO: the Extra is never drawn. No ink silhouette, outline, cast shadow, reflection, eyes or face, in any frame. A reviewer scrubs every shot for this before sign-off.

It can only SUBTRACT, in five ways: from the COUNT (seven piles, the sixth card, five fresh glasses, the fifth glass, five names for four people); from the COMPOSITION (a gap at Scott's right in every table shot); from the PAPER (knockouts to the backing fire); from TIME (acting only across cuts); and from SOUND (digital silence under its words).

GEOGRAPHY LOCK: everything it does happens in the gap sector at Scott's right, which is Kay's chair after she leaves (4 to 6 o'clock in top-down). In the yard it is frame-right of Scott, his free right-hand side. Scott's right is never given a clean, centred shot while something is happening there.

THE VOICE borrows the typeface of the friend whose line it is mimicking: 'Scott.' in Angelo's Oswald, the soft 'Angelo.' in Deena's Archivo Black. It is cut through the paper to the fire, at the empty corner. Nothing lands as Scott apparently saying his own name.

SCARS PERSIST PER SET. VOICE perforations stay on the dining table plane at 6%. The handprint and the throat arc stay in the kitchen, glowing 25% by the standoff and leaking ember around the edge of Angelo's jacket. The house literally leaks more fire as the night goes on.

THE HAND LADDER, a second-viewing echo, never a callout:
(1) The sixth hand presses the sixth card as unrimmed ink from the dark, LEFT hand, PRESS pose.
(2) The handprint is a LEFT-hand hole pressed into the blood beside Deena, at 35% knockout depth, with no flicker.
(3) The final hand is a LEFT hand of fire light clasping Scott's right hand on the grass.
The three poses are similar but not identical, with no rings and no rain beads, so the Kay reading ('Save my seat', 'Big night for you') stays alive beside the horror reading.

FAKE KAY obeys the doctrine. At the LATER game 'Kay' is only fragments (rain-bead glints along an ink edge against ink, a defocused edge, cards landing at her place). They step on twos, while the real Kay moved on ones. They cast no shadow and catch no rim. Her chair is tucked in. The lip-marked glass never moves and never empties.

VISIBILITY LADDER (it escalates with the story):
- L0: the second click, and a sixth footprint trail that begins inside the threshold.
- L1: seven misregistered piles.
- L2: the sixth hand.
- L3: the bottle and five glasses.
- L4: knockout VOICE letters, the first fire seen indoors.
- L5: the photo taken from Scott's right by no one.
- L6: the throat arc, the snap of the ponytail, the handprint hole.
- L7: the explosion's inversion frames, when the whole world briefly becomes its material.
- L8: a whole hand of light, held.
Its only musical identity is the 7th natural harmonic (384.7 Hz plus 385.3 Hz over a 55 Hz drone, about 31 cents flat of G4): one partial too many. It swells only when the Extra acts.

The final relief lands before the reveal. Warmth rises on Scott's face and his shoulders drop, then 'Two.' is spoken, and only after that does the camera find the hands. The wide shot that follows shows no second figure, only a small hand-shaped glow on the grass at his right.
counting_device:
THE LETTERBOX HEADCOUNT is the master counter, supported by four subordinate counts.

THE MATTES
- Look: two ink #0D0A09 bars, top and bottom. Their inner edges are hard and run through the same cut-paper edge noise (+/-0.7 px) as everything else. The bottom bar's inner edge carries the 10% dormant call line.
- Act 1 is full frame (1.78:1, no mattes).
- Behaviour: each step glides over 2000 ms on cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1), timed to the moment an absence is FELT or NOTICED, not when it happens:
  - Christof's crash (5:23.5): 1.85.
  - Scott's 'Where's Kay?' (5:50.5): 2.00.
  - Deena's last breath (9:32): 2.20.
  - The cut to Marina's empty doorway (9:48): 2.39.
  - The single-take standoff: a continuous squeeze from 2.39 to 2.76, until the frame is a slit holding two men and a lighter.
  - The explosion: the mattes burn away as paper strips (burn-through mask), and the yard plays full frame to the end.
- Type rule: from the 2.39 step onward, dialogue moves ONTO the mattes, so the dark edge of the frame becomes the page. Scott is in the top band; Angelo and everyone else are in the bottom band. At 2.39 each band is 138 px tall (one line up to 56 px). At 2.76 each band is 192 px (two lines at 52 px).
- How it lies:
  - It does NOT step at Kay's bathroom click, so it counts noticing, not loss.
  - During the LATER game it still shows full frame while 'six people apparently play', agreeing with a table that holds a fake.
  - It never closes for the Extra. In the yard, after 'Two.', the frame stays fully open.

SUBORDINATE COUNTS
(1) SPECULAR COUNTS. Highlights ping across a countable set at 6-frame intervals, each with a glass ping that steps +2% in pitch: six glasses on the counter, then six places at the table. This teaches the audience to count in Act 1. The same device later counts FIVE fresh glasses for us without anyone asking, a count that includes the Extra.

(2) COUNT CUTS. The six-card re-deal is six cuts of exactly 12 frames, landing on the groove's eighth notes. The second hand-count is four 10-frame whip pans across Scott, Deena, Marina and Angelo, then a fifth whip pan nobody asked for, which lands on the empty chair at Scott's right and holds 30 frames.

(3) ANGELO'S BLANK SLOT. When the table count is wrong, one wordless, card-width slot is dealt after his line with a snap. Its conspicuous absence after 'Perfect.' is the tell that this count only looks right.

(4) TALLY INTERSTITIALS, scratched card-paper marks on ink in a Kyle Cooper style, three in the film:
- After the second click: 30 frames. Six marks scratch in at 3-frame intervals, then a faint seventh appears at 25% and fades before it finishes; its scratch sound is dry, panned to Scott's right and pitched -100 cents.
- After 'Together.': four marks over 24 frames.
- The end card: two marks under the title. The second mark's scratch sound is dry and panned right like the second CLICK; visually the two marks are identical.

The tally records what the characters believe. The VOICE, the sixth hand and the ending show what the room holds.
motion_rules:
CADENCE:
- Master frame rate 24 fps. Characters animate on twos (pose time tq = floor(t*12)/12).
- Real Kay animates on ones.
- Panic beats switch to ones: Scott's legs giving way and his scream, Angelo catching Deena, Scott running, the blast throw.
- Camera, light, type, particles, grain and mattes always run on ones.

EASING LIBRARY:
- hover start (Scott): cubic-bezier(0.55,0.06,0.68,0.19) after a 3-frame anticipation.
- tidy settle: cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), 160 ms.
- snap (Deena): cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), 4 frames.
- deal (Angelo): cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1), 180 ms.
- Kay: cubic-bezier(0.37,0,0.63,1) at 1.25x duration.
- Christof gesture: cubic-bezier(0.34,1.4,0.64,1).
- Marina: cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1), no overshoot.
- camera moves: cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1).
- type exit fades: cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1), 200 ms.

CAMERA:
- Held-tension push-ins at 0.25-0.5% scale per second, linear.
- Table top-down: overhead rotation of 1.2 deg/s that stops dead (zero ease-out) on the 'Perfect.' deal.
- Snap zooms on shocks: 6-8 frames, cubic-bezier(0.7,0,0.84,0), +12% scale.
- Whip pans: 10 frames, cubic-bezier(0.83,0,0.17,1), with motion blur from 5 sub-frame samples at 20% each.
- Rack focus: per-plane cached ctx.filter blur from 0 to 8 px over 12 frames, cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1).

SHAKE:
- None in Act 1.
- From the hand circle: seeded value-noise drift of 0.6 px at 0.4 Hz.
- Kitchen: 1.5 px rising to 3 px, at 4-7 Hz.
- Crash: a 6 px one-frame jolt.
- Explosion: 18 px decaying exponentially (tau 300 ms, reaching zero by 1200 ms), plus a 2-frame 1.06x punch-in.
- The final ending shot is perfectly locked.

SHOT-LENGTH CURVE:
- Arrivals: average 4.5 s.
- Party: 4 s.
- Cards: 3.2 s.
- After the crash: 2.4 s.
- Hand circle: 2.0 s, with one cut per name.
- Kitchen: 1.3 s.
- Lighter standoff: ONE unbroken take of 54 s (10:29-11:23) on a 0.4%/s push from a medium two-shot to Angelo's thumb, with the matte squeeze the only other change.
- Explosion: cuts of 4-6 frames.
- Ending: holds of 10-18 s.

DIALOGUE SURVIVES CUTS: in any section where the average shot length is under 2.5 s, active lines are screen-anchored, not shot-anchored, and carry across cuts until their hold time is met. A shot may not end a line early.

HOLD RULE: every line holds max(0.9 s, 0.35 s + 55 ms per character) after its entrance completes. At most 3 lines on screen at once (2 inside the mattes). Entrances are 250 ms or less, except Kay and Marina, which are timed per character and stay under 700 ms, and Scott's caret typing (38 ms per character).

TYPE CONTRAST LINT: each line's glyph box is sampled against the quarter-res frame and must reach a WCAG contrast ratio of 4.5 or more. Failing lines get an automatic ink knock-behind: a rounded rectangle of #0D0A09 at 70% opacity with a 24 px feather. Type never sits on tungsten or hood-yellow light bands. Minimum type size is 44 px.

MATTE-AWARE LAYOUT: no glyph may ever fall under a matte. Below 2.39 the type lives in the live area with a 48 px safe inset. From 2.39 onward it moves onto the matte bands (Scott top, everyone else bottom), x-aligned to the speaker and clamped 96 px from the frame edges.

SPATIAL DISCIPLINE:
- Act 1 strictly obeys the 180-degree rule.
- The hand circle deliberately breaks it, covering four people from five sides as if the table had a fifth seat.
- Returning to a master set-up uses the IDENTICAL camera, so an absence is legible.
- Characters turn across cuts, Reiniger-style, and are never rotated in 3D.
PARALLAX: each master has 3-5 depth planes moving at factors 0.2 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.3. Deeper planes are lifted 6% toward the key colour for atmospheric perspective.
EDGE BOIL: the cut-paper edge noise is frozen through Act 1. From the hand circle it re-seeds every 2 frames at +/-0.4 px, rising linearly to +/-1.4 px by the oven. In the yard it is frozen again.
intensity_devices:
MASTER CURVE (ink share / aspect / average shot length / heartbeat bpm / gas hiss):
- Party: 40% / 1.78 / 4.5 s / none / none.
- Cards: 55% / 1.78 / 3.2 s / 60 bpm at -34 dB.
- After the crash: 70% / 1.85-2.00 / 2.4 s / 80 bpm / hiss -54 to -47 dBFS (subliminal).
- Hand circle: 75% / 2.00 / 2.0 s / 88 bpm.
- Kitchen: 85% / 2.00-2.39 / 1.3 s / 96 bpm at -24 dB / hiss -30 to -18 dBFS.
- Standoff: 92% / 2.39 to 2.76 / one 54 s take / heartbeat replaced by hiss at -12 dBFS.
- Explosion: everything at maximum, then released.
- Ending: full frame / holds / two heartbeats locking.
THE LETTERBOX HEADCOUNT closes one step per noticed loss, then squeezes continuously through the standoff. It is almost subliminal, and the frame physically runs out of room.

VACUUM SILENCES of 0.4-1.2 s of true digital silence: before the gasp, under each VOICE word, as the oven door drops, at the throat (gas hiss drops out for 1 s), and before the final lighter scrape. Silence is the loudest cue in the film.

THE GROOVE GAINS A BEAT: the diegetic 6/8 party groove adds a seventh eighth (a rim click) in every bar after the second CLICK. After the crash it starts dropping seeded beats, and it stops dead on the oven door.

SUBLIMINAL GAS: the hiss enters at -54 dBFS on the frame Christof walks into the kitchen and rises about 2 dB per minute, unexplained, until 'What's that smell?' turns it from a sound into a recognition.

SOURING COUNTS: every count ping in the film is detuned a further 4 cents flat than the one before (global tick index). Any count past the true number gets an extra -100 cents, a completely dry signal and a +0.6 pan toward Scott's right.
EDGE BOIL: the silhouette outlines loosen from the hand circle onward (+/-0.4 rising to +/-1.4 px), so the outline of reality goes soft just as the counting fails.

TYPE PRESSURE:
- Lines grow and collide as the night goes on: Christof and Marina's comic collision at the door, then 'Christof.' and 'Kay.' landing on the same spot after the photo.
- Scott's width narrows in notches. Angelo's dealing decays through flicked, dropped, undealt and chrome stages. Christof's bulbs fail. Marina's grid shakes apart. Deena's slam goes soft.
- In the standoff the type thins to almost nothing.
RIM-LIGHT THINNING: Angelo's rim drains from 4 px to 1 px over 3 s as his smile goes. In the kitchen every rim is 1-2 px: the light is leaving them.
PERSISTENT SCARS: the Extra's knockouts never heal. By the standoff the dark kitchen glows faintly from the handprint and the throat cut, so the horror accumulates on screen.
WINE FLASHES: 2-frame wine multiplies at 25%, used only 3 times (crash, throat, spark), each separated by at least 1 s from any other flash event.

RISING SOUND FLOOR:
- Fridge hum steps from -40 to -28 dB on the cut after the soft 'Angelo.', reaching -22 dB in the corridor.
- Heartbeat climbs from 60 to 96 bpm.
- The 7th-harmonic leitmotif swells every time the Extra acts.
THE FIRST LONG TAKE: after a kitchen cut at 1.3 s average, the 54-second unbroken standoff push is unbearable stillness. Its first cut, Scott running, is the release.
THE SECOND HEARTBEAT: in the yard, a second lub-dub, panned +0.5 to Scott's right and out of phase, drifts in period until it locks exactly with Scott's on 'Two.'

sound_palette.web_audio_recipe:
Rendering: each scene renders in its own OfflineAudioContext(2, ceil(48000*dur), 48000) from the same cue table as render(t). Scenes are concatenated with 50 ms equal-power crossfades into one 48 kHz WAV, then muxed. A single 14-minute context would need about 320 MB of float buffers.

Noise: all noise comes from mulberry32-seeded AudioBuffers.

Buses: room, music, fx, landing, score (drone, leitmotif, heartbeat), tinnitus. All feed a master DynamicsCompressor (threshold -16 dB, ratio 4, attack 0.004 s, release 0.22 s), then the destination.

Reverbs: ConvolverNodes whose impulse response is stereo, decorrelated, seeded noise multiplied by exp(-6.9t/RT). RT values: living room 0.5 s, corridor 0.8 s, kitchen 0.25 s (bright tile), yard 2.8 s.

Preview: scrubbing plays the pre-rendered WAV from an offset with an AudioBufferSourceNode.

Two sine OscillatorNodes at 6200 Hz and 6205.5 Hz (a 5.5 Hz beat), each through a gain of 0.008.
- Cold open: a 2 s linear fade-in, sitting at -38 dBFS under the fire.
- After the blast: it returns at -26 dBFS for 5 s while a master BiquadFilter lowpass drops to 700 Hz (Q 0.7), then both recover with setTargetAtTime (tau 4 s, lowpass back to 18 kHz).

Roar: a seeded brown-noise buffer (b = (b + 0.02*w)/1.02, scaled x3.5), looped, through a lowpass at 700 Hz (Q 0.5), gain 0.22, with a 0.13 Hz LFO at 30% depth on the gain. Add sines at 41 Hz and 62 Hz at -30 dB with 0.2 Hz amplitude modulation.

Crackle: a precomputed seeded Poisson schedule at lambda = 10 per second. Each event is a 4-15 ms white-noise burst through a bandpass at a random 2.5-4.5 kHz (Q 2) with an exponential decay (tau 8 ms).

Pops: 1-2 per second, each 30 ms of noise through a lowpass at 1.2 kHz.

sound_palette.cue: Room tone, party walla and the laugh that cuts off
sound_palette.web_audio_recipe:
Room tone: sines at 50 Hz (gain 0.010) and 100 Hz (0.006), plus brown noise through a lowpass at 200 Hz at -42 dB.

Walla: 6 decorrelated pink-noise streams. Each passes through three parallel formant bandpasses (500 / 1500 / 2500 Hz, Q 4) with seeded syllabic amplitude modulation at 4-6 Hz, then a lowpass at 3 kHz, at -34 dB, panned -0.6 to +0.6.

Laughs: bursts of the same streams with amplitude modulation at 7-9 Hz and the formants gliding up 15% over 300 ms. On 'Maybe you don't get to play.' a laugh starts at +0.4 s and is cut to 0 in 10 ms after 350 ms.

White noise through a highpass at 1.2 kHz and a lowpass held at 1.5 kHz while the door is shut. When the door opens, the lowpass ramps to 7 kHz and the gain rises +12 dB over 150 ms; this reverses when it shuts.

Droplets: seeded impulses at about 30 per second, each a 2 ms noise burst through a bandpass at 4 kHz, with a random StereoPanner position from -0.6 to 0.6.

Tempo: dotted-quarter at 70 bpm, so one eighth note = 285.7 ms. Chords Dm9, G13, Cmaj9, A7(b9), one per bar.

FM e-piano: a sine carrier plus a sine modulator at the same frequency feeding carrier.frequency. Its deviation envelope falls from 3.0x to 0.6x the note frequency over 350 ms. Amplitude envelope: 6 ms attack, 1.6 s decay. Tremolo 4.8 Hz at 0.12 depth.

Rhythm section:
- Bass: triangle wave through a lowpass at 400 Hz.
- Kick: a sine sweeping 120 -> 48 Hz in 60 ms, 180 ms decay.
- Brush: white noise through a bandpass at 6.5 kHz (Q 0.8), 2 ms attack, 90 ms decay, with eighth-note velocities [1, .4, .6, .8, .4, .6].

The seventh beat: after the second CLICK, every bar gains a seventh eighth, a rim click (3 ms of noise through a bandpass at 1.8 kHz, Q 6, velocity 0.5).

Life of the groove: heard from the next room it goes through a lowpass at 900 Hz. After the crash, seeded one-beat dropouts occur at p = 0.25. It stops dead on the oven door frame.

Doorbell: a sine at E5 (659.25 Hz), then C5 (523.25 Hz) 400 ms later. Partials at x2.0 (-12 dB) and x3.0 (-20 dB), exponential decay over 1.2 s, through the room reverb.

Knock: a sine sweeping 95 -> 60 Hz over 40 ms, plus 30 ms of noise through a lowpass at 800 Hz. The impatient knocking is 3 hits, 180 ms apart.

First CLICK: 4 ms of noise through a highpass at 3 kHz into a bandpass at 2.1 kHz (Q 12), 25 ms decay, panned -0.3, sent to the room reverb.

Second CLICK: the identical recipe, but completely DRY, panned +0.6 (Scott's right) and 1.5 dB quieter. The same sound, from the wrong place.

The bathroom-door CLICK uses the first-CLICK recipe through the corridor reverb at -6 dB.

Flick: 6 ms of white noise through a bandpass at 3.2 kHz (Q 2), plus a 15 ms sine 'thup' at 160 Hz.

Slap: 20 ms of noise through a lowpass at 1.5 kHz, 50 ms decay.

Riffle: 40 flick grains over 0.8 s, with the gap between them accelerating from 35 ms to 12 ms, then slowing again.

Timing: the slaps of the six-card re-deal land exactly on groove eighths. A blank slot gets a slap with no flick.

Each ping is inharmonic sines at 2.8, 4.1, 5.9 and 7.3 kHz with gains 1, 0.6, 0.35, 0.2 and an exponential decay of 600 ms.

Pitch rules:
- Within one count, each ping steps +2% in pitch, 6 frames apart.
- Every ping is also multiplied by 2^(-4n/1200), where n is the global ping index, so the film's roughly 50 pings sink about 200 cents.
- A ping past the true number gets an extra x 2^(-100/1200), no reverb and a +0.6 pan.

sound_palette.cue: Dialogue landing sounds, one per speaker (-30 to -38 dBFS)
sound_palette.web_audio_recipe:
Everything sits at -30 to -38 dBFS so it reads as texture, not as game chirps.
- Scott: per character, a haptic tick (sine at 180 Hz, 6 ms, exponential decay, -42 dB). Deletion is the same tick at 220 Hz and -48 dB.
- Deena: a knuckle knock (sine 180 -> 120 Hz over 25 ms, plus a 3 ms noise tick).
- Angelo: a card snap (the flick recipe at half level). It stops at stage S4.
- Kay: a water drip (sine sweeping 1.4 -> 2.4 kHz in 40 ms, 80 ms decay).
- Christof: a bulb tink per word (sines at 1760 Hz and 2640 Hz, 120 ms).
- Marina: a key tick per glyph (0.8 ms click at -44 dB), plus a glass-on-coaster tap when the line completes (inharmonic sines at 2.9, 4.4 and 6.1 kHz, 250 ms).
- Dispatcher: a 2 ms gate click per line, over a narrowband line bed (pink noise through a highpass at 300 Hz and a lowpass at 3.4 kHz, -42 dB) with seeded 20 ms dropouts.

The drone: sines at 55*n Hz for n = 1..6, each at gain 1/n, master level -28 dB, with a 0.05 Hz breathing lowpass between 300 and 900 Hz.

The Extra's partial: n = 7, a detuned pair at 384.7 Hz and 385.3 Hz, normally at gain 0.

Swells: whenever the Extra acts, the pair swells to -20 dB over 1.5 s and decays over 4 s. The triggers are the second click, pile seven, the sixth hand, the bottle, both VOICE words, the phone handover, the throat and the handprint.

In the ending it is the last tone left under the fire, and it crossfades into the two-voice unison.

sound_palette.cue: VOICE (O.S.): the hole in the sound
sound_palette.web_audio_recipe:
For each VOICE word:
1. A 150 ms reversed swell of the room-tone buffer, ramping 0 to +4 dB.
2. Every bus EXCEPT the 7th-harmonic pair is set to exactly 0 with setValueAtTime(0, t0), held for the word's on-screen duration (about 0.9 s).
3. The buses return over 300 ms with linearRampToValueAtTime.
There is no landing sound and no reverb.

On the cut after the soft 'Angelo.' the fridge hum jumps +12 dB.

Each beat is a 'lub' (sine at 52 Hz, 8 ms attack, 120 ms decay) followed 210 ms later by a 'dub' (sine at 44 Hz, 4 dB quieter), through a lowpass at 150 Hz.

Tempo is scheduled from the cue table: it enters at the seven hands at 60 bpm, -34 dB, then goes to 72 at the skipped card, 80 after the crash, 88 at the hand circle and 96 in the kitchen at -24 dB. It is replaced by the hiss in the standoff, then returns in the yard at 84 and settles to 72.

The second heartbeat: the same recipe at 4 dB quieter, panned +0.5. It starts at 'How many people made it out?' at 64 bpm, out of phase. Its period is interpolated linearly so that its beat coincides with Scott's exactly on the 'Two.' frame, and the two stay locked afterwards.

A 50 Hz sawtooth through a lowpass at 180 Hz (Q 2), plus a 100 Hz sine at -6 dB, with 0.2 Hz amplitude modulation for the compressor motor. It sits at -40 dB, steps to -28 dB on the cut after the soft 'Angelo.' and reaches -22 dB in the corridor.

Two decorrelated white-noise buffers, hard-panned left and right, through a highpass at 2.8 kHz and a peaking boost of +6 dB at 6.5 kHz (Q 1). A 7 Hz sine LFO flutters the gain at 8% depth.

Gain automation:
- -54 dBFS on the frame Christof enters the kitchen, rising 2 dB per minute.
- -30 dBFS at 'What's that smell?'
- -18 dBFS at the oven.
- Silent for 1 s at the throat, then back louder.
- -12 dBFS through the standoff.
In the kitchen add a second layer through a bandpass at 9 kHz (Q 4), slightly offset in level so the two beat.

sound_palette.cue: Christof's gasp and the metallic crash
sound_palette.web_audio_recipe:
First, 0.5 s of vacuum (all buses at 0).

Gasp: noise through two parallel bandpasses (700 Hz, Q 8; 1200 Hz, Q 10). The envelope rises over 60 ms and is cut to 0 at 180 ms, so it sounds choked off.

Crash, 120 ms later: eight sine partials at 320 Hz x [1, 2.76, 5.40, 8.93, 13.34, 18.64, 24.6, 31.4] with seeded gains and exponential decays of 0.4-1.6 s, plus a 60 ms noise burst and a 70 Hz thud. It plays through the kitchen reverb, then a 'wall' lowpass at 4 kHz, so it sounds heard through a wall.

Thump: a sine sweeping 110 -> 70 Hz over 80 ms, plus noise through a lowpass at 600 Hz. Dry, panned +0.6.

Glasses: five souring count pings, 6 frames apart, with the 7th-harmonic swell under them.

Charge whine: a sine sweeping exponentially from 2 kHz to 9 kHz over 1.2 s at -42 dB.

Shutter: two 5 ms noise clicks, 70 ms apart, through bandpasses at 1.8 kHz and 2.4 kHz (Q 8).

On the white frames, all ambience ducks 12 dB for 6 frames.

sound_palette.cue: Oven door, bulb buzz, stove shift
sound_palette.web_audio_recipe:
Stove shift (the 'damp, ugly sound'): brown noise through a bandpass sweeping 220 -> 110 Hz (Q 4) over 450 ms, plus a 55 Hz thud.

Oven door: 0.6 s of total silence first. Then an 80 Hz sawtooth with 6 Hz FM (+/-8 Hz) through a lowpass at 900 Hz for 600 ms, plus a hinge squeal (sine 1.2 -> 0.9 kHz). The groove stops on this frame.

Bulb buzz: a 100 Hz square wave through a lowpass at 800 Hz at -32 dB, gated in sync with the visual flicker.

sound_palette.cue: Scott's scream, carried by the waveform
sound_palette.web_audio_recipe:
No voice synthesis.
- A thin breath: noise through a bandpass at 900 Hz (Q 4), 400 ms.
- Then nine sawtooth oscillators around 220 Hz, detuned +/-25 cents, through a lowpass sweeping 300 Hz -> 4.5 kHz over 1.5 s (Q 6), into a WaveShaper soft clip (tanh(4x)), with the tinnitus pair rising underneath.
Its envelope drives the dormant call line's waveform bars. It is cut dead on the cut to Deena.

The gas hiss drops to 0 for 1 s.

Paper tear: white noise through a bandpass sweeping 4.5 -> 1.4 kHz over 300 ms (Q 3), gated by a seeded random on/off pattern of 2-6 ms, like fibres tearing: the paper world being cut.

Ponytail jerk: a 55 Hz sine for 80 ms plus a noise whoosh through a bandpass sweeping 400 -> 2400 Hz in 90 ms.

Wet flutter: noise through a lowpass at 420 Hz, amplitude-modulated at 70% depth by a square LFO slowing from 9 Hz to 4 Hz, decaying over 2.5 s and then stopping.

Wheel scrape: 6-8 grains of 2 ms noise at 45 per second through a bandpass at 5 kHz (Q 3).

Failed spark: a 3 ms bright click (highpass at 6 kHz) plus an 80 ms sizzle (noise through a highpass at 8 kHz, exponential decay), with no flame tail.

The final scrape heard from the yard is the same patch, dry and dead centre, in 0.4 s of total silence.

First, 0.4 s of digital silence after the scrape. Then:
- Boom: a sine sweeping exponentially 34 -> 18 Hz over 1.2 s at full scale, plus a brown-noise burst through a lowpass at 180 Hz with a 3 s decay.
- Crack: 80 ms of unfiltered white noise.
- Glass: 60 seeded inharmonic pings (3-9 kHz, 80-300 ms) scattered over 1.5 s.
- The master compressor goes to a 20:1 ratio for 1 s.
- The tinnitus pair and the 700 Hz master lowpass take over for 5 s, then the fire bed fades up.
- The second explosion follows 3 s later: the boom 8 dB quieter, plus 400 ember crackles.

DTMF tones: each digit is two summed sines for 120 ms at -24 dB ('9' = 852 + 1477 Hz, '8' = 852 + 1336 Hz, '6' = 770 + 1477 Hz).

The two misdials: '9 9 8' then a delete blip, '9 6' then a delete blip. The delete blip is a 4 ms sine at 2 kHz.

Then '9 9 9' and the UK ringback: 400 Hz + 450 Hz summed, cadence 0.4 s on / 0.2 s off / 0.4 s on / 2.0 s off, through the phone band (highpass at 300 Hz, lowpass at 3.4 kHz).

The line connects with a 2 ms click; the timer starts on that frame.

A distant UK two-tone: a triangle wave alternating 770 / 960 Hz every 0.6 s (setValueAtTime) with a +/-10 cent Doppler drift, through a lowpass at 1.2 kHz and the yard reverb at -32 dB, creeping 6 dB louder over 60 s, panned -0.3.

Under it, a faint relay tick (2 ms click at -46 dB) in sync with each change of strobe colour.

Each mark is 60 ms of noise through a bandpass at 3.5 kHz (Q 2), amplitude-modulated by a 30 Hz square wave.
- The faint seventh mark, and the second end-card mark: dry, panned +0.6; the seventh is also -100 cents.

On 'Two.' two sines at 220.0 Hz and 220.6 Hz (beating every 1.7 s) fade in to -26 dB over 3 s, while the 7th-harmonic pair fades out over 4 s.

In the last 6 s everything else fades; the unison pair and the locked heartbeats go last, ending on the frame the hand's light reaches 0.

M12 yard close. Scott in profile facing screen-left, phone in his LEFT hand at his left ear, phone-white rim. His free right hand is cropped at frame-right, where a 6% warm flicker lives. The Dispatcher band and timer (00:01:37) sit in the upper third.

beat_map.scene: INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EARLIER
beat_map.beat: A hand scoops crisps from a bag into a bowl. Half miss; Scott picks them up and puts them in anyway. SIX glasses. SIX places at the table.
beat_map.visual:
M13 top-down in a warm tungsten pool. The crisps bounce as card-paper flecks.
- A lateral push across six glass silhouettes on the counter: a specular count pings 1 to 6 at 6-frame intervals.

beat_map.beat: Title sequence: ONE TOO MANY, Screenplay by Osita Miles.
beat_map.visual: The six glasses match-cut into six ink bars on a tungsten field, their widths hinting at the six bodies (Angelo's the tallest). The bars land on 6/8 beats with card slaps, then shuffle apart to make room for a seventh that never arrives. In that empty slot 'ONE' appears in Six Caps, knocked out to fire for 1 s. 'TOO MANY' sets across the bars in tungsten. The credit is in Barlow Condensed 600, tracked +200. The dormant 1 px call line begins along the bottom edge.

beat_map.beat: The doorbell; Deena and Angelo (six-pack, unlit cigarette). 'You moved the sofa.' through 'It's decorative.'
beat_map.visual:
M1 front door, locked off and symmetrical; every arrival plays in this exact frame. The door opens on rain-slate night with rain-silver streaks and a rain swell.
- Deena's Archivo Black lines slam on.
- Angelo's 'You know who's coming tonight, right?' is dealt phrase by phrase.
- Comic beat: he takes the cigarette down, finds nowhere to put it, puts it back, and 'It's decorative.' is dealt at a jaunty 2 deg.

beat_map.beat: KNOCK: Kay with dripping ice, rain beads in her hair. 'Before you tell me I didn't need to bring anything--' through 'No, no. I'll take it.' The almost-question moment. Then Deena O.S. 'Kay! Save yourself. He's rearranged the whole room.', the furniture-polish exchange, 'It really does.'
beat_map.visual:
M1. Kay animates on ones; rain beads glint on her hair edge and the ice bag drips.
- Scott's silhouette blocks the doorway until she nudges past.
- Graphic-eye close-up E1: their two profiles nose to nose, with a bare amber caret blinking between them and no text.
- Deena's O.S. line slides in from frame-left, already cropped.
- Kay sniffs; her italic writes on and leaves a lipstick last glyph.

beat_map.beat: RING plus impatient KNOCKING: Christof and Marina arrive mid-argument (the second light, the two churches). Angelo O.S. 'Finally! You two coming in or what?' 'See? Two people heard that address and only one got us lost.' 'She's been rehearsing that in the car.'

beat_map.beat: Scott shuts the door. The latch CLICKS, then a second quiet CLICK as his hand leaves it. He checks the lock; it is secure. He lets it go.
beat_map.visual:
Insert: the bolt slides home. Scott's hand leaves the latch, then the second CLICK plays (dry, panned right) over a frame that does not change for 36 frames. The 7th harmonic breathes in; the groove gains its seventh beat from here. The lock check is a hand insert.

beat_map.scene: INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - LATER
beat_map.beat: Music, wet footprints by the door, everyone talking. Christof's biscuit story ('I thought it was a date. That's my point.' through 'It was a twelve-quid drink.'). Marina wipes a wine ring and Scott hands her a coaster: 'Thank you. The table's going to live.' / 'It's a borrowed table.' / 'That explains the tension.'

M2 at the warmest light of the film. Out of focus by the door: five trails of wet prints from the mat, and a sixth trail that begins a metre INSIDE the threshold.
- Christof's marquee: 'twelve-quid drink' grows to 1.4x; Angelo deals 'That's not a reason.'
- M13 top-down: the ringed hand wipes a crisp wine ring in a 1.4 Hz circle, and a card-paper coaster lands circle-on-circle. Marina's ring draws round 'live'.

beat_map.scene: INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - LATER
beat_map.beat: Kay in the kitchen doorway: 'Sit down, Scott.' / 'I'm sitting.' / 'You're standing.' Scott glances at his legs, sits on the couch arm. 'Better.' Deena almost comments. Angelo pulls the deck: 'Are we doing this, then?' / 'You liked that story.' / 'I liked when it ended.'

Kay leans 8 deg inside the bright kitchen doorway, still warm here.
- Scott makes a 4-frame head dip to his own legs, then a perch with a tidy correction.

beat_map.scene: INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - DINING AREA - MOMENTS LATER
beat_map.beat: Gathering at the table. Deena swaps Angelo's glass with her own; Christof drags a chair for Marina; Angelo's poor-magician flourish. 'Just deal them.' / 'Can I enjoy something?' / 'Not in this house, apparently.'

M4 profile two-shot of Scott and Kay, with cards crossing the background as motion-smear rectangles and table banter defocused behind them.

beat_map.scene: INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - DINING AREA - LATER
beat_map.beat: Six piles now. Six people apparently playing; Kay never in clear view, her chair tucked in. Christof wins: 'Thank you. I'll accept apologies individually.' through 'Your cards are awful. Why would I?' 'There's another in the kitchen. Left cupboard.' Christof goes through to the kitchen.
beat_map.visual:
M3 and M4 at full frame, so the frame 'agrees' with six players. FAKE KAY as fragments only: rain-bead glints on an ink edge behind Christof's shoulder, a defocused edge behind a glass, cards landing at her place across cuts. They step on twos, with no shadow and no rim. The lip-marked glass never moves.
- Christof walks into the hood-yellow doorway and the glare swallows his curls.
- 'And don't touch my cards.' stays at 20% over his empty chair; his biscuit stays on the table.
- The gas hiss enters at -54 dBFS.

beat_map.beat: Scott taps Kay's glass: first pour, a small red lip mark, hardly any wine gone. From the kitchen, a short choking GASP. A METALLIC CRASH. Everyone jolts.
beat_map.visual:
Insert: the rim with the lip mark, the most saturated thing in frame. The tap rings and sustains into the drone.
- 0.5 s of vacuum, then the gasp and the crash.
- On one frame every silhouette jumps to a startle pose, with a 6 px camera jolt and a wine flash.
- The lamp drains to tungsten-tired. The matte steps to 1.85 over 2 s. The groove starts dropping beats.

beat_map.beat: 'Christof?' No response. 'What was that?' Scott steps toward the kitchen; a bottle comes down behind him with a soft THUMP. 'Scott, you're standing on my foot.' / 'Sorry.' He looks down, moves; when he looks up the bottle is there, and five fresh glasses. 'Oh. Thanks.' No one answers. He pours. 'That's plenty.' / 'Sorry. Just tell me when.' / 'I did. Twice.'
beat_map.visual:
'Christof?' shrinks in perspective down M5 into the doorway glare, unanswered.
- Insert: his socks on her shoe.
- Cut back up: the bottle (its highlight catches Christof's green) and five glasses in a row, which a count pings 1-5 for us. The 7th harmonic swells.
- 'Oh. Thanks.' sits in a caret silence aimed at the gap.
- The pour is a flat wine ribbon that overfills.

beat_map.beat: 'Where's Kay?' through 'Maybe she was.' Then 'We'll start when Christof gets back.' / 'He did come back.' / 'He went to get the wine.' / 'Yeah. This wine.' They all look at the bottle. 'Probably went for a smoke.' / 'He doesn't smoke.' / 'Then I don't know, Scott.' Nobody admits how long they've avoided the kitchen door. 'We can do one quick hand. Until they come back.' / 'Both of them?' / 'Yeah. Kay and Christof.'
beat_map.visual:
The matte steps to 2.00 on 'Where's Kay?'
- M6 corridor: the door is closed and the light line is steady, with no feet.
- An insert of the bottle in Scott's hand as every eyeline converges on it.
- A long hold on the M5 kitchen doorway that nobody looks at.
- Scott nods: it sounds right, then a micro-acting brow knit, then it doesn't.

beat_map.scene: INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - DINING AREA - CONTINUOUS
beat_map.beat: Four piles, then a FIFTH. Deena catches his wrist: 'Angelo. Stop.' / 'What?' / 'Count those.' Five. Scott. Deena. Marina. Himself. 'No.' / 'What?' His chair scrapes back. 'Is somebody messing with me?'
beat_map.visual:
Christof's dim marquee goes dark on the first card.
- Insert: Deena's hand closes on his wrist, a two-hand silhouette. Her pointer rule touches the fifth pile, set at the gap.
- Count cuts: four 10-frame whip pans, then a fifth that lands on the empty chair at Scott's right and holds 30 frames, with its tick flat and dry.
- A blank slot follows 'What?'. A hard chair scrape.

beat_map.beat: 'Nobody's touching the cards except you.' / 'That's what I'm saying.' / 'Angelo, sit down.' / 'No, hang on. Just-- hands. Give me your hands.' / 'What are you doing?' / 'I want to count the people. Not the cards. Just give me your hand, Scott.' / 'You're actually scaring me now.' He softens. 'I'm not trying to. Come on. It'll take ten seconds.'
beat_map.visual: Angelo's phrases now drop from above (stage S3). Deena's 'You're actually scaring me now.' is in Archivo 500 with no shake. Angelo's rim warms back to 2 px as he softens. Handheld drift begins and edge boil starts. The heartbeat rises to 88.

beat_map.beat: They link hands: four people. Scott's left in Marina's warm, ringed hand; his right in a hand he takes for Angelo's. 'All right. Just say who's on your left. Don't let go. Somebody start.' VOICE (O.S.): 'Scott.' Scott doesn't react. 'Marina.' 'Deena.' 'Angelo.' 'Scott.' The names hang in the room.
beat_map.visual:
M3 top-down: a four-body ring whose Scott-to-Angelo link stretches long over Kay's empty place, a kink rather than a fifth body.
- Inserts: ring glints in Scott's left hand; his right holds a long-fingered hand at the rim of the light.
- 'Scott.' is cut through the table at 4 o'clock in Angelo's Oswald, glowing fire, while every bus drops to digital silence.
- Each name lands at its speaker's corner in their own face and colour, building a ring of five names round four people.

beat_map.beat: 'Wait.' / 'What?' / 'Didn't somebody already say me?' / 'I just did.' / 'No. Before that.' / 'Yeah. I heard it.' Angelo's grip tightens. 'Okay. Other way. Right this time.' / 'Angelo--' / 'Just do it.' 'Angelo.' 'Deena.' 'Marina.' 'Scott.' Scott can't make the circle fit.
beat_map.visual: The coverage breaks the 180-degree line: the circle is shot from five sides, one cut per name. The names build the ring the other way. The VOICE scar sits at 6% in the table. A close-up of the hands as Scott looks from face to face.

beat_map.beat: VOICE (O.S.), very softly: 'Angelo.' No one moves. 'Who said that?' The refrigerator suddenly feels loud. 'Scott, whose hand have you got?' He is holding Angelo's hand, of course. But a FIFTH wineglass sits between them on a coaster. 'Why's that there?' / 'Don't let go yet.' Marina lets go; they all break contact at once.
beat_map.visual:
The soft 'Angelo.' is cut through at 30 px and 60% depth, in Deena's Archivo Black, at the empty corner. On the next cut the fridge jumps +12 dB.
- Close-up: Angelo's long-fingered hand, now rim-lit.
- Pull back to reveal the fifth glass on a coaster at 4 o'clock, with a rack focus to it.
- Every hand releases on the same frame.

Scott, Deena, Angelo and Marina against the wall; Marina's hand trembles on Scott's shoulder. A CAMERA SHUTTER. The phone is back in Marina's hand.
beat_map.visual:
Marina's grid sentences each take their own row.
- Insert: her ringed hand holds the glowing phone out toward frame-right (Scott's right) while her head stays turned away. The phone is gone across the cut.
- A wide of the four, framed from exactly the photographer's spot at a lens height of 1.5 m. The ring glints flicker at 7 Hz.

- Cut: the phone is in her hand.

beat_map.beat: Four people in the photo; none holding the phone. 'Four. There's four of us.' / 'I can see that.' Angelo zooms. 'Who took it?' / 'Christof.' / 'Kay.' (at once). 'No. I gave it to--' She looks at her own hand. 'Kay's in the bathroom.' / 'And Christof's in the kitchen.' / 'Then let's go get them.' / 'Together.'

- 'Christof.' and 'Kay.' land on the same spot and interpenetrate, readable by colour.

M6 corridor lit only by the far kitchen glow. Four silhouettes walk away, and four long shadows stretch back toward the lens (count them).
- Kay's 8% 'Big night for you.' sits on the wall.
- Insert: Scott's hand stops 40 px short of the handle, and the afterimage dies on that exact frame. The under-door line is unbroken, with no feet.
- Marina's tiny grid line.

beat_map.beat: Empty kitchen; a cupboard open, a chair pushed out. 'Christof?' A quiet HISS. 'What's that smell?' Two burner knobs missing, broken plastic under the cabinet. 'Oh, shit. Gas.' through 'I'm trying.' The stove shifts with a damp, ugly sound. 'Leave it. We'll get outside and call someone.' / 'Just one second.'

M7: a hood-yellow cone over the stove, ink and soot checker tiles, the open cupboard a black rectangle, a gas-blue haze shimmering.
- Insert: the row of knobs, two of them bare spindles (count them), and card-paper shards under the cabinet.

- Handheld 1.5-3 px. Average shot length 1.3 s, with screen-anchored type carrying across cuts. Angelo slides in at stage S5.

beat_map.beat: His hand finds the oven handle. 'Scott, don't--' He opens it. CHRISTOF is folded inside the oven, his head crushed against the back wall, blood pooled beneath. Scott makes a small sound, his legs give way, then the screaming starts. 'Oh, God. Oh, God--' / 'No. No, no--'

The oven door's falling edge slices Deena's line in half. 0.6 s of silence; the groove stops dead.
- The bulb throws hard under-light. The FIRST image is a huge distorted shadow of the folded body thrown across the ceiling.
- Then an 18-frame insert: the rig folded past its joint limits, the curl cloud flattened against the wall with crease lines, a bent knee and a palm-up hand separated by the bulb's rim, three drops over the lip.

- Marina's grid shakes apart; Angelo's phrases drop.

beat_map.beat: Deena grabs Scott's shoulders; he turns to her. For an instant she's fine. Then her throat OPENS. No knife. No figure. She clamps her palms over it, her eyes fix on Angelo, and something JERKS her head upright as she tries to fall.
beat_map.visual:
Profile two-shot against the oven light.
- Frames 0-12: still.
- Frame 12: a 1 px knockout ARC across the FRONT of the throat (about 80 px, stopping well before the nape), the paper itself cut.
- Frames 12-16: it widens to 4 px glowing ember.
- Frame 14: her ponytail tip snaps 40 px straight up toward an empty point and her head jerks 8 deg.
- Frames 16-20: the glow floods to blood with three short runs; a wine flash.
- The hiss drops out under the paper tear.
- Graphic-eye close-up E5: her eye fixed on Angelo, disbelieving. First view under 1 s.

beat_map.beat: 'Dee?' He almost slips in the blood and catches her before the tiles. 'Hey. Hey, look at me. Look at me.' A wet, desperate flutter. 'No, no. Stay. Come on, Dee. Come on.' Her body goes quiet. Angelo holds her anyway.
beat_map.visual: A low angle: Angelo's silhouette folds over hers, on ones. His card-blue phrases slide rather than deal. Her ink palms over the arc, with red glowing between her fingers like a rim. The flutter slows from 9 Hz to 4 Hz and stops. On her last breath the matte steps to 2.20. Her type never appears again.

beat_map.beat: Scott backs into the counter and grabs a kitchen knife; his hand won't stop shaking. 'Where is it?' / 'What?' / 'There was-- something had her. I saw her hair--' / 'I didn't see anybody.' / 'I know.'
beat_map.visual: The blade is the brightest line in frame, trembling at 9 Hz. 'Where is it?' is set at 72 px, condensed, tracking -40. A whip-pan sweep of the dark kitchen finds nothing. 'I saw her hair--' is guillotined at the dash.

beat_map.beat: 'Marina? Marina, get away from the door.' No answer: Marina is gone. 'Marina?' / 'She was here. She was just here.' Blood beside Deena, pressed into the shape of a hand; no hand remains. 'I was holding her.' / 'I know.' / 'I was right there.' / 'Angelo, we need to go.' / 'Then how did it--' / 'We go out the back. Now. Come on.'
beat_map.visual:
Cut to M5 in the exact framing where we saw her four shots earlier: an empty, dim amber rectangle, with only her last wine-ring full stop hanging in it, no text. The matte steps to 2.39 and dialogue moves onto the mattes.
- Scott can't put his back to Angelo, so a standoff two-shot holds.
- M9 top-down on the tiles: a LEFT-hand-shaped hole pressed into the blood pool at 35% knockout depth, glowing faintly, with no flicker.

beat_map.beat: Angelo lays Deena down and covers her throat with his jacket, far too late. 'When you counted us. You kept saying five.' / 'What?' / 'The cards. The picture. I thought I was--' / 'Don't. Don't think about that. We get outside.' / 'And whoever did this just comes with us?' The HISS grows louder. 'The gas. Angelo, we have to shut the gas off.' Angelo looks at the stove, then at Deena.
beat_map.visual:
His silhouette visibly thins as the jacket comes off. The jacket's edge is rim-lit from beneath by the scar's ember glow.
- Scott glances over his shoulder toward the empty hallway.
- Graphic-eye close-up E6: Angelo's look from the stove to Deena.

beat_map.beat: He drops the cigarette and takes out a cheap metal LIGHTER. 'No.' / 'Back door's there.' / 'Put it down.' / 'Go, Scott.' / 'Just-- think for one second.' / 'I have.' / 'Come with me. We can call the police from outside.' / 'And say what?' / 'I don't know.' / 'Neither do I.' / 'You always keep the back gate unlocked?' / 'Yeah.' / 'Good. Go through it. Don't stop in the yard.' / 'Angelo--' / 'Scott. Please.' / 'I don't want you here when I do it.' / 'You don't have to--' / 'Go.' A long beat. 'Sorry about your house.' His thumb strikes: a SPARK that fails.
beat_map.visual:
ONE unbroken 54 s take on a 0.4%/s push from a low two-shot (Angelo at the cone's edge, the back-door rectangle behind Scott, Deena's covered shape between them) to Angelo's thumb on the wheel.
- The cigarette leaves his silhouette and falls over 36 frames on ones, coming to rest at the edge of the blood.
- The matte squeezes continuously from 2.39 to 2.76. Scott's lines sit in the top matte; Angelo's in the bottom.
- From 'Scott. Please.' Angelo's lines turn to chrome Oswald 300. 'Sorry about your house.' is a face-down card that flips over 18 frames.
- The thumb strikes: 2 frames of six radial spark strokes, then a wine flash.

beat_map.beat: Scott runs. He flies through the door, nearly falls down the steps, grabs the handle to pull it shut. From inside: the tiny, dry SCRAPE of a lighter wheel.
beat_map.visual: A whip cut to M10, the back door from outside. Scott bursts out as a silhouette in the light rectangle on ones and stumbles. The rectangle narrows to a slit as the door shuts, mirroring the front door. Through the glass, a small Angelo with the lighter raised. 0.4 s of total silence, then the scrape.

beat_map.beat: The kitchen ERUPTS. The blast throws Scott down the steps; windows burst outward; heat washes the grass. His shirt catches; he rolls until the fire dies. He crawls to the far fence, coughing and sobbing. A second explosion. For a while, nothing he can do but watch.
beat_map.visual:
The explosion, frame by frame:
- Frames 0-2: dark.
- Frames 3-5: blast-white.
- Frames 6-9: inversion, so the world briefly becomes the Extra's material.
- Frame 10 onward: full fire. 60 glass triangles burst out; the mattes burn away as paper strips; 500 grass blades flatten at 900 px/s; a shake of 18 px decaying to 0.
Then Scott is thrown in 4-frame cuts, rolls through three poses until the flame tongues die, and crawls to the fence. The second blast throws 400 embers. Hold a 6 s locked wide, with the gap open at his right.

beat_map.beat: Flames eat the upstairs; red lights strobe faintly through the fence. Scott has found his phone; his thumb shakes so badly he misses the emergency number twice. The call connects.
beat_map.visual:
M11, then M12. Strobe bars (red and blue at 0.8 Hz each, at most 20% of screen area) slide through the fence slats.
- M14 keypad insert: a grid of glowing digits; his ink thumb misses ('9 9 8' then delete; '9 6' then delete).
- Then 9 9 9 and the ringback. The timer starts at 00:00:00 on connect at t = 724.0. The dormant call line brightens.

beat_map.beat: 'Emergency services. What is your address?' He gives it, barely getting the words out. 'Are you injured?' / 'Yeah. I-- yeah.' / 'Help is coming. Is anybody still inside?' A window collapses inward. 'My friends.' / 'How many friends?' / 'Five. I had five over.' / 'And are they all still inside?'
beat_map.visual: The Dispatcher's fixed band and running timer in the upper third. Scott's lines are typed in ash, extra-condensed. The address is five ash redaction bars, typed and deleted. A window collapses in an M11 cutaway. Fire rims Scott's back.

beat_map.beat: He tries to count. Deena. Christof. Angelo. Kay. Marina. He can't make the numbers stay still. 'I don't know. I don't know where-- I don't know.' / 'Sir, listen to me. You're outside. You're safe for now.'
beat_map.visual:
Five names rise around him in their owners' faces at 60% (as images of his memory, not dialogue), with a sixth, letterless slot cut through as a faint knockout bar. They orbit along Angelo's dealing arc.
- Interleaved count-cut inserts, one per name: Deena's hoop, Christof's biscuit, Angelo's dropped cigarette, Kay's lip-marked glass, Marina's ring glints. The inserts shuffle out of order.
- On his line the names scatter off-frame like thrown cards. The Dispatcher's line is steady.

beat_map.beat: 'How many people made it out?' Scott wipes his face on his sleeve. 'Me.' A pause. Something warm closes around his free hand. He doesn't look down; he squeezes back. Relief, so sudden it hurts. 'Two.'
beat_map.visual:
'Me.' is typed at 140 ms per character, 160 px ash, extra-condensed, in the night sky, never deleted. Then 2 s of fire.
- Graphic-eye close-up E7: warmth rises on the right side of his face from frame-right, a second warm catchlight appears, and the brow releases.
- Medium: his forearm tenses and his shoulders drop 6 px. The second heartbeat locks.
- 'Two.' types in amber at normal width; the caret stops and vanishes. Timer 00:00:54.

beat_map.scene: EXT. SCOTT'S BACK YARD - LATER / END
beat_map.beat: He lowers the phone a little. On the grass beside him: THEIR HANDS, held tight. No second figure is visible. The house burns. The two hands do not separate. FADE OUT. THE END.
beat_map.visual:
The camera tilts down and widens 20% over 4 s. Scott's ink right hand is clasped by a LEFT hand made of fire seen through a hand-shaped knockout; its wrist dissolves into the grass within a third of a forearm.
- A wide: Scott alone, with a small hand-shaped glow on the grass at his right and no figure.
- Back to the hands: an 18 s hold on a 0.2%/s push, the house soft behind (6 px blur), strobe crossing both hands.
- Everything sinks to ink over 4 s; the hand is the last light.
- End card at 814 s: 'ONE TOO MANY' in Six Caps, with two tally marks scratching in, one then the other.

The guillotine is kept for interrupted dashes. A bare caret blinks in his silences with Kay. The cold open cuts on the seventh blink. 'Two.' is the only Scott line never deleted.

ONE ROD TOO MANY: a second heartbeat, panned to Scott's right and out of phase, drifts into exact lockstep on 'Two.' It sits under the two-sine unison.

ONE ROD TOO MANY and RECOUNT: Angelo's full break is keyed to 'Scott. Please.' His dealing decays through flicked, crooked, dropped, undealt and sliding stages. His final 'Sorry about your house.' is a face-down card that flips over 18 frames.
RECOUNT: 'Big night for you.' leaves an 8% afterimage on the corridor wall that dies on the exact frame Scott's hand stops short of the bathroom handle.
RECOUNT: after Marina vanishes, her last wine-ring full stop hangs alone, with no text, in the empty doorway. Also from RECOUNT, the ring drawn around a key word ('live').

ONE ROD TOO MANY: left-behind objects. Christof's biscuit and his dim 20% marquee 'And don't touch my cards.' stay over his empty chair. In the ending count, one insert per name, shuffled out of order.
RECOUNT: the gas hiss starts subliminally at -54 dBFS the moment Christof enters the kitchen and rises 2 dB per minute.
RECOUNT: the dormant 1 px call line from the title onward. It wakes once as Scott's scream, clipping red, then becomes the call in the yard.
RECOUNT: count ticks sour, 4 cents flatter per use across the film, with an extra -100 cents and a dry right-side pan on any count past the true number.
ONE ROD TOO MANY: the lighter standoff as one unbroken 54 s push, with the matte squeeze inside the take. Its first cut is Scott running.
ONE ROD TOO MANY: the deterministic low-res burn-through mask for the cold-open slit, the curtain, and the mattes burning away in the explosion.
